messages:
maria (eng-sre): Heads-up: multiple hosted customers reporting 503s and tracer shows upstream inference worker processes dying during high-concurrency model loads. Seeing both GPU OOM and segfaults.
kevin (eng-runtime): Observed same in our perf cluster. Start times align with model swap + high QPS. Repro steps? :thinking_face:
sanjay (eng-ml): Could be KV prefetch / attention kernel path when context length spikes. I have a failing trace from one customer run.
tara (support): Customer A opened a ticket — they saw 503s starting ~15:22 UTC, heavy retry loop, then billing spike from retries. They want ETA/fix.
ben (oncall): Putting a temporary mitigation: will route traffic off the problematic pool and enable fallback model for affected tenants. Doing now.
ops-bot: reroute-task: started hot-route to fallback-model-v1 for tenant: cust-a
maria (eng-sre): Paste of the tail of the worker log just before crash:
```
[2026-03-17T15:22:31Z] INFO infer: starting request id=ri_9a2f
[2026-03-17T15:22:31Z] WARN kv_prefetch: miss count=312
[2026-03-17T15:22:31Z] ERROR runtime: GPU out of memory when allocating 128MB (device=0)
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
```
kevin (eng-runtime): For another host we see segfault stack:
```
#0 0x7f9c2a3b in aten::native_conv()
#1 0x55f1d4c3 in Runner::forward()
#2 0x55f1d9a7 in main_infer_loop()
```
kevin (eng-runtime): Looks like a mixed failure surface: some are OOMs, some are illegal instruction / segfaults. Could be kernel mismatch or a bad quantized op landing after model swap.
sanjay (eng-ml): Which model version rolled out recently? We did a quick swap of opt-quant-v3 yesterday to serve latency improvements.
maria (eng-sre): Yes, opt-quant-v3 was swapped onto the main pool at 15:10 UTC. Canary looked OK but only tiny traffic.
ben (oncall): I grabbed node metrics: GPU memory usage climbs to >98% and then process killed by oom_killer on the host in a couple cases. Also one kernel panic trace on a driver reset.
nathan (infra): Driver versions across pool nodes: some are 525.85, others 525.89; there's a known minor nv driver reset bug in 525.85 with certain PTX patterns.
kevin (eng-runtime): We should immediately pause further swaps and roll affected nodes to the stable driver 525.89. Also pin customers to pre-swap model for 30m.
tara (support): Customer A wants a concrete mitigation: can we provide a rollback and credits? They reported high retries increased cost.
maria (eng-sre): Mitigation plan (short):
- take pool out of LB (ben) :white_check_mark:
- pin affected tenants to opt-quant-v2 (kevin) :white_check_mark:
- drain and repro on isolated node with debug symbols (sanjay + kevin)
- roll driver to 525.89 on nodes that exhibited resets (nathan)
- support to communicate status + provisional credit plan (tara)
kevin (eng-runtime): Repro command we used locally (recreates high-concurrency prefix + long context):
```
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST $RR_API -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"model":"opt-quant-v3","input":"'$(yes "hello" | head -n 2000 | tr -d '\n')'"}' &
done
```
ben (oncall): While draining pool I saw one container restart with exit code 139 (SIGSEGV) then next attempt got OOM. We'll collect coredump and logs to S3: s3://redwood-dumps/3823456790/
maria (eng-sre): Sanjay — can you run gdb/bt on coredump and check if it's in a specific op (attention or fused matmul)?
sanjay (eng-ml): On it. Early bt shows crash inside fused_attention_backward_impl, possibly a shape/quantization mismatch. Will attach summary shortly.
ops-bot: debug-upload: logs uploaded to s3://redwood-dumps/3823456790/ (size 124MB)
kevin (eng-runtime): Quick config mitigation: reduce per-worker max-concurrency from 16 -> 8 and max-batch-tokens from 4096 -> 2048 for opt-quant-v3 pools. This should reduce peak allocation and avoid OOMs.
ben (oncall): Applied concurrency throttle on pool: pool-id=u-3f7a, changed worker.concurrency=8. Observing a drop in OOM triggers in last 3min.
maria (eng-sre): Tara please tell Customer A: we rolled them to opt-quant-v2, throttled concurrency on their pool, and are investigating root cause. We'll also issue a credit for retry consumption while we fix.
tara (support): Sending update to customer now. Drafting: "We mitigated by routing your traffic to a stable model version and throttling peak concurrency. We're investigating root cause and will follow up in 2-4 hours with a detailed postmortem." Will cc legal for credits.
kevin (eng-runtime): Longer-term actions:
- revert opt-quant-v3 canary (block further rollout)
- add kernel-level guards around fused_attention calls for shape assertions
- add unit test that exercises long-context with opt-quant-v3 quantization path
- add driver version gating to rollout pipelines
maria (eng-sre): Sanjay, prioritize backtrace + minimal repro that triggers segfault in CI, we need deterministic test to run before any quantized rollout.
sanjay (eng-ml): Will try to produce deterministic repro within 90min. Early hypothesis: a rare race when KV cache growth crosses a page boundary combined with a specific PTX path in opt-quant-v3.
nathan (infra): I'll schedule rolling nodes to 525.89 tomorrow morning GMT+1; if needed we can hotpatch now but prefer controlled roll.
ben (oncall): Next steps I did:
- created incident ticket INC-382345 (internal)
- pinned metrics alert to higher sensitivity (mem/driver-resets)
- coredumps + kernel logs collected
- tentative severity: P1 until we confirm limited blast radius
maria (eng-sre): Good. After sanjay attaches bt, we'll decide on rollback vs guarded re-enable. Thanks team. :heart:
kevin (eng-runtime): Note for postmortem — include billing exposure calc (retry multiplier) and customer impact window.
tara (support): Customer A confirmed fallback is working and latency improved. They're appreciating the quick reroute. I'll keep them updated.
maria (eng-sre): Closing loop: last observed 503 for that tenant at 15:29 UTC after reroute. Marking last_message_ts accordingly.
